title: Photography and Hyper-Realism
answer: Synthetic portraiture, lighting rigs, upscaling, product mockups and virtual location scouting.

children.name: Synthetic Portraiture
children.blurb: Synthetic portraiture is the creation of lifelike images of human faces and figures using generative image models rather than a camera.

children.name: Lighting Rigs and Relighting
children.blurb: Lighting rigs and relighting in AI image generation cover the placement, color, intensity, and falloff of virtual lights, and the process of changing the illumination in an existing photograph or render.

children.name: Upscaling and Noise Reduction
children.blurb: Upscaling and noise reduction in photography and hyper-realism covers the processes that increase image resolution and remove grain, sensor noise, or compression artifacts while preserving or enhancing fine detail.

children.name: Product and Fashion Mockups
children.blurb: Product and fashion mockups use AI image generation to create photorealistic previews of clothing, accessories, packaging, and other goods without a physical photo shoot.

children.name: Virtual Location Scouting
children.blurb: Virtual location scouting uses generative image and video models to produce photorealistic previews of potential filming locations before a physical recce.

sections.body: This section covers the practical use of image generation models for photographic and hyper-realistic output. The site tracks 1000 live image generation models, and the pages here describe the subset applied to synthetic portraiture, lighting control, upscaling, product mockups, and location scouting. Current work is not theoretical, these models are producing still images used in casting tests, e-commerce drafts, and previsualization. The focus is on outputs that read as photographs rather than illustrations, with attention to skin texture, lens behavior, and scene geometry.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The strongest results are in static, single-subject images with controlled prompts. Synthetic portraiture can now produce convincing faces at moderate resolution, but consistent identity across multiple shots remains unsolved. Lighting rigs and relighting work well for broad mood changes, yet fine physical accuracy, like correct shadow softness from a specific softbox, is still limited. Upscaling and noise reduction are mature for two to four times enlargement, but they can invent texture that was not in the original file. Product and fashion mockups are useful for early layout decisions, not for final color-accurate catalog work. Virtual location scouting gives a rough sense of a space, but measurements and repeatable camera moves are not reliable.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would begin with Synthetic Portraiture to understand how models create faces and the limits of identity consistency. From there, Lighting Rigs and Relighting explains how to change illumination after capture or during generation, which matters for matching a portrait to a scene. Upscaling and Noise Reduction covers the final cleanup step, turning a low resolution or noisy render into a cleaner still. Product and Fashion Mockups applies the same techniques to commercial still life and apparel, where surface detail and fabric drape are the main concerns. Virtual Location Scouting extends the workflow outward, using generated environments as stand-ins for real sets before a shoot.
